frozen_denominator.reconciliation: No discovery replay. All seven frozen Source Families have final states: five exact-v1 Full Source Reviews and two identity/date/rejection closures. All exact-v1 arXiv HTML sources were accessible; no access blocker remains.

deep_analysis_selection.rationale: These three change durable system contracts at distinct boundaries: runtime tensor placement under transient device load, persistent near-memory capacity co-design, and protocol-valid evaluation of reusable KV compression. ABot-AgentOS and GRASP still receive complete standard Source Reviews; narrative selection does not downgrade their evidence state.

full_source_reviews.title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Exact paper v1 with implementation design, equations/algorithms, author experiments and ablations; no author implementation repository linked in v1

locators.artifact: No author repository is linked in exact v1; llama.cpp and Hugging Face Accelerate are cited dependencies, not ATSInfer provenance

full_source_reviews.problem: Consumer-device models exceed GPU memory, but conventional layer/expert offload assumes tensors inside a layer have similar residency value and that CPU/GPU/PCIe performance remains stable. At batch one, transient background load and thermal throttling can reverse the best placement during a request.
full_source_reviews.old_solution_and_constraint_change: Layer-level static offload is simple, predictable and amortizes profiling when the machine is dedicated and operator behavior is homogeneous. It becomes wasteful when tensors have different CPU/GPU speedup per byte and when local CPU, GPU or PCIe availability changes while prefill and decode share one device.
full_source_reviews.mechanism: Profile per-tensor CPU/GPU execution and transfer costs, solve a memory-constrained static placement using measured performance density, keep nonresident tensors in pinned host memory, overlap Copy-Engine and SM-driven Zero-Copy transfers with computation, then observe realized transfer/compute time and re-run dynamic placement only after deviation and rate-limit thresholds are crossed. Prefill and decode retain distinct plans because their compute/memory balance differs.
full_source_reviews.state_ownership_and_flow: The execution-plan owner binds model/tensor identity, dtype/layout, per-backend kernels, GPU-resident region, pinned-host state and temporary buffers. The runtime owns measured CPU/GPU/PCIe load and may propose a new physical placement; it must not alter tensor semantics. Graph rebuild and dynamic-program decisions are versioned transitions, and in-flight execution must not observe a partially switched plan.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_and_failure_modes: Tensor granularity improves use of scarce GPU bytes and runtime load feedback avoids a stale plan, but adds profiling, pinned memory, buffer reservation, graph rebuild, dynamic-program and hysteresis policy. Re-scheduling too often costs a material fraction of TPOT; too slowly leaves a stale plan. Thermal drift, unsupported kernels/formats, PCIe contention and inaccurate profiles can erase gains. Static layer placement remains preferable for stable dedicated hosts, small models, strict predictability or insufficient telemetry.

benchmark_contract.model: Laptop: GLM-Z1-9B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, GPT-OSS-20B; desktop: Llama3.1-70B, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, GPT-OSS-120B
benchmark_contract.hardware: Laptop Intel i7-11800H + RTX 3060 6GB + 32GB DDR4 + PCIe Gen4 x16; desktop Intel i7-11700 + RTX 4090 24GB + 64GB DDR4 + PCIe Gen4 x16
benchmark_contract.precision: GLM-Z1-9B FP16; GPT-OSS native MXFP4; remaining models INT4
benchmark_contract.output_length: Decode 128 tokens; sustained laptop study varies 32-2048 tokens
benchmark_contract.batch_or_concurrency: Batch size 1; common local interactive setting, not multi-tenant serving
benchmark_contract.slo: No production tail SLO; throughput, TPOT, GPU SM utilization and effective PCIe bandwidth reported under the paper's setup
benchmark_contract.baselines: llama.cpp, vLLM 0.18.0 and KTransformers 0.5.2 with model/format support gaps disclosed
benchmark_contract.reported_result: Author reports up to 1.94x prefill and 3.29x decode throughput improvement; load-aware adaptation reduces TPOT increase by 13% at 60% CPU load and 38% under combined 60% GPU/PCIe pressure in reported cases
benchmark_contract.claim_boundary: Evidence supports the measured consumer platforms and batch-1 models/formats only; it does not prove fleet-wide tail latency, energy, concurrency, portability or correctness under arbitrary background load

full_source_reviews.books_patch_proposal: In Ch49, after the existing hybrid-backend execution-plan boundary, add an evolution chain: coarse layer/expert offload -> profiled per-tensor placement -> asynchronous transfer/computation overlap -> runtime load observation -> hysteresis/rate-limited plan transition. State explicitly that the scheduler owns physical placement, not tensor semantics; bind profile/model/dtype/layout/hardware identity; preserve static placement for stable hosts. Add a short handoff to Ch54 for pinned-host/GPU/temp-buffer budget and Ch56/Ch63 for host-load and placement observability. Do not copy the paper's product name or peak speedups into the stable mechanism paragraph.

full_source_reviews.title: FlashAccel: Leveraging High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) for High-Throughput LLM Inference
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Exact paper v1 with hardware/system co-design, event-driven simulation, sensitivity/ablation and appendix calculations; proposed hardware is simulated, not fabricated

locators.artifact: No FlashAccel implementation or simulator repository linked in exact v1; cited GitHub pages are dependency/background sources

full_source_reviews.problem: HBM capacity caps resident weights and KV cache, so batch/concurrency can remain capacity-bound even when compute and bandwidth could support more work. Ordinary flash provides persistence and capacity but its page latency, access granularity and poor parallel utilization make naive GPU attachment unsuitable for the latency-critical path.
full_source_reviews.old_solution_and_constraint_change: HBM-only residency gives the simplest latency and consistency contract; host/NVMe offload is cheaper and deployable but often exposes a slow transfer boundary. The constraint changes when flash can be integrated at HBM-like aggregate bandwidth and its latency hidden by die-level parallelism, SRAM prefetch and layout-aware scheduling.
full_source_reviews.mechanism: Co-design an HBF stack and GPU attachment, distribute small SRAM buffers close to flash planes, map weights and KV into layouts that expose plane-level parallelism, prefetch future pages without stalling dependent kernels, and use an HBF-aware storage/programming layer to coordinate persistent and HBM/SRAM state. Capacity permits larger SLO-bounded batches; bandwidth and page latency remain the limiting constraints.
full_source_reviews.state_ownership_and_flow: Persistent HBF stores versioned weight/KV pages, while HBM/SRAM are execution caches. The storage manager owns logical-to-physical mapping, placement, prefetch and release; kernels consume the current mapping but do not own persistence. Page-table updates must preserve a valid fallback Flash address until prefetch commits. KV lifecycle, request isolation and write ownership cannot be inferred from capacity alone.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_and_failure_modes: The design exchanges new die/packaging area, SRAM, controller complexity, specialized layouts, simulator uncertainty, endurance/write amplification and heterogeneous fault recovery for much higher resident capacity. Strict SLOs can make lower-bandwidth configurations underperform HBM; hot mutable state may be a poor flash fit. HBM remains appropriate for hot latency-critical state, while conventional host/storage tiers remain preferable when new hardware is unavailable or persistence writes dominate.

benchmark_contract.hardware: Modelled DGX-H200 baseline (8 H200, six 141GB HBM3e stacks/GPU as paper config) versus 4/8-GPU CSI/CLI designs with modelled HBF; each HBF stack 192GB Flash, 32MB SRAM, 768GB/s
benchmark_contract.precision: FP16 except DeepSeek-V3 weights in FP8
benchmark_contract.input_length: LongProc-derived 8.11K and agentic 15K average input lengths
benchmark_contract.output_length: LongProc-derived 2.53K and agentic 6K average output lengths
benchmark_contract.batch_or_concurrency: Largest simulated batch satisfying capacity and decode-latency constraint; varies by model/configuration
benchmark_contract.slo: 50ms and 100ms per decode step (approximately 20 and 10 tokens/s/user as paper states)
benchmark_contract.simulation: Event-driven LLMCompass/ScaleSim-based GPU model extended with plane-granularity NAND latency; technology parameters derived from cited XL-Flash/area sources
benchmark_contract.reported_result: 8-GPU CSI averages 2.15x throughput/GPU over 8xH200 in the detailed results; abstract reports 2.54x average throughput/GPU and 1.93x energy efficiency for six-HBF integration across its aggregate evaluation
benchmark_contract.claim_boundary: All end-to-end gains are simulator/model outputs under assumed HBF characteristics, layouts and SLOs; they are not measurements from fabricated HBF hardware and do not establish endurance, yield, reliability or production tail behavior

full_source_reviews.books_patch_proposal: Extend Ch54's '异构近数据与池化状态' after the existing CXL/near-memory branch with a distinct persistent near-memory branch: HBM-only -> conventional offload -> bandwidth-near persistent flash + SRAM/layout/prefetch -> SLO-bounded batch expansion. Separate persistent owner from execution caches; require technology/simulator calibration, page-layout identity, commit/fallback mapping, endurance/write and failure accounting. Preserve HBM for hot state and explicitly label the evidence simulated. Ch49 receives only a short execution-plan handoff; do not promote HBF as a deployed default.

full_source_reviews.title: How Query Visibility Changes KV-Cache Compression Rankings: A Matched-Budget Audit
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Exact audit paper v1 with matched-pair records, bootstrap analysis, robustness checks, explicit withdrawals and limitations; implementation uses NVIDIA kvpress 0.5.4 and paper states release of harness/records, but v1 links only the upstream repository

locators.artifact: https://github.com/NVIDIA/kvpress (audited upstream implementation, version 0.5.4); no immutable author harness/records locator is linked in exact v1 HTML

full_source_reviews.problem: KV-compression rankings often evaluate with the question visible before compression, while reusable prefix caches must be compressed before any future query is known. That protocol mismatch can reward query relevance rather than reusable information retention; backend and tokenizer differences can exceed method gaps.
full_source_reviews.old_solution_and_constraint_change: Query-aware compression is valid when each request owns a one-shot prompt and query, because the query is available to select relevant KV. It is invalid as evidence for shared/reusable cache compression, whose state must commit before downstream queries arrive. A benchmark label such as 8192 also ceases to be comparable when tokenizer expansion exceeds a model's positional budget.
full_source_reviews.mechanism: Freeze identical models, instances, compression budgets and decoding; vary only whether the query is visible at compression time; compare each method against several trivial start/recent baselines with paired bootstrap; keep the attention backend fixed; run uncompressed and backend controls; quarantine tokenizer-invalid rows; withdraw rankings whose method requires a backend with a measured effect larger than method gaps.
full_source_reviews.state_ownership_and_flow: The deployment lifecycle owns when cache state becomes reusable and therefore which information is legally visible to the compressor. The method owns a selection score but not the evaluation protocol. The harness owns tokenizer-expanded length, backend, budget, implementation revision and exclusions. A leaderboard may publish a ranking only after these identities and matched controls are committed.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_and_failure_modes: Matched deployment protocols improve external validity but can exclude methods incompatible with the common backend or single-pass harness. Trivial baselines prevent false novelty but do not prove the winner is optimal. Backend numerical divergence, tokenizer overflow, OOM refill, lineage similarity and uniform ratios can silently reshape rankings. Query-aware evaluation remains appropriate for nonreusable per-query caches; query-agnostic evaluation is required for reusable caches.

benchmark_contract.model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; gemma-2-9B quarantined/disqualified for tokenizer-expanded positional overflow
benchmark_contract.precision: Paper reports backend numerical effects; portable dtype/accumulation contract is not fully disclosed in the headline
benchmark_contract.input_length: RULER nominal 8192 plus LongBench natural-text tasks; tokenizer-expanded length explicitly checked
benchmark_contract.output_length: Task-specific; fixed within matched pairs, not a serving throughput benchmark
benchmark_contract.batch_or_concurrency: Offline paired audit; no production concurrency/SLO
benchmark_contract.protocol: Query-aware vs query-agnostic compression, six kvpress 0.5.4 methods, three trivial baselines, two ratios, paired comparisons and 50,000-resample bootstrap
benchmark_contract.records: 144,300 RULER paired evaluations and 40,800 LongBench records; abstract/conclusion state 185,700 paired records overall
benchmark_contract.reported_result: SnapKV protocol delta +0.198 versus KeyDiff +0.011; under query-agnostic RULER SnapKV trails the best trivial baseline by 0.066 on average. Switching sdpa/eager shifts pooled results substantially, including -0.29 uncompressed RULER accuracy in the highlighted control, so H2O ranking is withdrawn
benchmark_contract.claim_boundary: Supports protocol sensitivity for the audited implementations, models, 8K RULER/LongBench and uniform budgets. It does not rank all KV compressors, resolve H2O, validate 32K-128K reuse, or establish the paper's ordinal visibility hypothesis causally

full_source_reviews.books_patch_proposal: In Ch66 near matched-budget/counterfactual protocol design, add a reusable-state evaluation invariant: freeze the production visibility/commit boundary before scoring; match model/tokenizer-expanded length/backend/implementation revision/budget; include uncompressed and trivial controls; measure harness/backend effects and withdraw rankings when the confound is comparable to method gaps. Add one short handoff in Ch45: query-aware retention and query-agnostic reusable-prefix retention answer different deployment questions and must not share a leaderboard claim. Preserve query-aware methods for one-shot request-owned caches.

full_source_reviews.title: ABot-AgentOS: A General Robotic Agent OS with Lifelong Multi-modal Memory
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Exact paper v1 plus author project page; initial subset agent evaluation and heterogeneous memory benchmarks, with several model-judged metrics and unreleased/private production components

locators.artifact: https://amap-cvlab.github.io/ABot-AgentOS (author project page; v1 states complete benchmark release is future work and private data/production results are not released)

full_source_reviews.problem: A VLM/VLA controller can map observations to actions, but long-horizon embodied work also needs durable task state, skill delegation, verification/recovery, cross-embodiment interfaces and memory that binds observations, identities, space, time and provenance.
full_source_reviews.old_solution_and_constraint_change: A single controller and prompt-local memory are reasonable for short tasks and one embodiment. Long trajectories, dynamic events and repeated interaction create context drift, premature termination and untraceable updates; directly coupling reasoning to low-level control also makes hardware transfer expensive.
full_source_reviews.mechanism: Insert a deliberative harness above low-level controllers; isolate skill contexts; maintain structured task state; verify stage and terminal conditions; store multimodal observations/traces as typed provenance-bound graph memory; diagnose failures after evaluation and promote derived evo-assets only to later splits. Edge/cloud separation attempts to keep private memory local while sharing common knowledge.
full_source_reviews.state_ownership_and_flow: Low-level controllers own physical execution; the Agent harness owns plan/skill/verification workflow state; raw observations and traces remain authoritative evidence; graph memory is a derived indexed view; self-evolution assets are optimizer-owned candidates and gain authority only after later-split gates. Post-hoc labels never belong in the current split's inference context.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_and_failure_modes: Hierarchy and persistent memory improve auditability and recovery but add skill-interface drift, verifier error, cross-store synchronization, privacy/access control and stale derived assets. Benchmark feedback can become leakage without split-order enforcement. The reported real-world/benchmark scope remains limited; noisy perception, actuation, network latency, safety and heterogeneous embodiments are not closed. A monolithic controller remains simpler for short, reversible, well-observed tasks.

benchmark_contract.model: Agent subset compares Qwen3.6-Plus single controller, Qwen3.6-Plus hierarchical system and DeepSeek-V4-Pro hierarchical system; common Qwen3-VL-Plus observation tool. Memory benchmarks use benchmark-specific GPT-5.4/Qwen3.6-Plus/Qwen3.5-Flash roles
benchmark_contract.hardware: Not disclosed as a reproducible systems benchmark
benchmark_contract.input_length: Task/benchmark dependent; not disclosed as a common contract
benchmark_contract.batch_or_concurrency: Offline agent/memory evaluations; no production concurrency
benchmark_contract.datasets: Initial EmbodiedWorldBench subset plus LoCoMo, OpenEQA, Mem-Gallery, NExT-QA and EgoLife; raw scores are kept dataset-specific
benchmark_contract.reported_result: On the initial subset, Qwen3.6-Plus hierarchical system reports TSR 61.96%/GCR 68.79% versus 49.97%/57.95% for the single-controller baseline. Memory results and self-evolution gains are benchmark-specific and include LLM judges
benchmark_contract.claim_boundary: Initial validation, not a complete leaderboard or large-scale physical deployment. Base models differ across memory tasks; private production data/results and the full benchmark are not released in v1

full_source_reviews.books_patch_proposal: No mechanism patch. Ch81 already separates durable workflow state, typed transitions, skill execution, verification and external-effect evidence; Ch77 already treats graph memory and failure-derived rules as provenance-bound, reversible derived state with held-out promotion; Ch26 owns physical controller/safety boundaries. A review-note citation may be added later, but repeating the architecture would create a second owner.

full_source_reviews.title: GRASP: GRanularity-Aware Search Policy for Agentic RAG
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Exact paper v1 with method, training details, three-benchmark evaluation, qualitative analysis and controlled ablations; no author code/checkpoint artifact linked in v1

locators.artifact: No author repository/checkpoint linked in exact v1; Search-R1 Hugging Face collection is a baseline artifact, not GRASP provenance

full_source_reviews.problem: Static or single-tool Agentic RAG fixes retrieval signal and context unit, so broad semantic exploration, exact entity lookup and local verification compete inside one interface. Retrieving full paragraphs early also injects distractors and weakens the next-query signal.
full_source_reviews.old_solution_and_constraint_change: A fixed dense or lexical top-k retriever is inexpensive, reproducible and effective for homogeneous short QA. Multi-hop problems change the state: different reasoning stages need different matching signals, and sentence-level discovery may need a later paragraph dereference rather than immediate full-context packing.
full_source_reviews.mechanism: Expose semantic-search, keyword-search and read-parent-paragraph actions. Return sentence-level hits with parent metadata, let the policy expand a selected clue, and train a GRPO policy with answer, grounded-reading, complementary-search and turn-efficiency rewards. Retrieval observations are masked out of the policy loss; the model learns an explore/exact-match/verify sequence rather than a fixed fusion rule.
full_source_reviews.state_ownership_and_flow: Retrievers own ranked evidence under their index revisions; the agent owns action selection and query state; read_chunk dereferences a parent but does not change source authority. Reward components observe gold annotations only during training and may not leak into deployment. The final answer requires separate evidence sufficiency/faithfulness checks.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_and_failure_modes: Adaptive tools and granularity can reduce irrelevant context and improve recall, but add tool calls, RL cost, reward shaping and premature-stop risk. Gold supporting facts make the reward nonportable; complementary-search rewards can encourage both tools even when one suffices. The result is shown on one 3B backbone and multi-hop QA corpora, not arbitrary enterprise RAG. Static hybrid retrieval remains preferable for low-latency or shallow tasks.

benchmark_contract.model: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct policy; BM25 lexical retriever; Qwen3-0.6B semantic retriever; Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B in the single-step hybrid baseline; gpt5-mini used for IRCoT trace generation and LLM judge
benchmark_contract.hardware: Full-parameter GRPO training on 2x NVIDIA A100 80GB; retrieval tools isolated on a third GPU node
benchmark_contract.input_length: Dataset/task dependent; no fixed token length disclosed
benchmark_contract.output_length: Multi-turn tool trajectories; final run stabilizes near eight tool calls/trajectory, but token length not disclosed
benchmark_contract.batch_or_concurrency: Training batch size 64; 270 GRPO steps (~17,280 prompts, ~19% of an epoch). Evaluation samples 500 validation questions/dataset, seed 42
benchmark_contract.slo: None; retrieval/QA quality rather than online latency
benchmark_contract.datasets: Train HotpotQA distractor; evaluate HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and MuSiQue with top-k=5 retrieval
benchmark_contract.metrics: Retrieval recall; EM, token F1 and binary gpt5-mini judge; ablation uses a 5,500-example HotpotQA subset with modified rewards
benchmark_contract.claim_boundary: Supports learned tool/granularity coordination on the stated 3B model and annotated multi-hop QA setup. It does not establish scaling, production latency, annotation-free rewards, calibrated stopping or resistance to hostile corpora

full_source_reviews.books_patch_proposal: No mechanism patch. Ch76 already owns hybrid lexical/dense routing, modality/operator-native retrieval, coarse-to-fine evidence interaction, query/compression/verification/stopping as a joint policy, and separates retrieval relevance from sufficiency. GRASP is a bounded experimental instance of that line. If desired, add only a Review-note citation with its gold-evidence/3B/latency limitations; do not repeat the method in stable prose.

closure_reviews.title: On the Efficiency of LoRA Fine-Tuning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Industrial Robotic Manipulation
closure_reviews.evidence_level: Exact arXiv v1 identity/date and abstract-level scope closure; below Full Review threshold and no override trigger
closure_reviews.disposition: Rejected — Low Durability / Out of Scope
closure_reviews.reason: A task-specific comparison of LoRA efficiency for industrial VLA manipulation does not introduce a new long-lived system mechanism beyond the existing PEFT and embodied-controller boundaries. Any reported efficiency is tied to its model, robot tasks and fine-tuning setup; no Books conclusion is changed.

closure_reviews.title: ActiveFly-Bench: Aligning Embodied Question Answering with Vision-Language-Action for Aerial Embodied Perception
closure_reviews.evidence_level: Exact arXiv v1 identity/date and abstract-level scope closure; below Full Review threshold and no override trigger
closure_reviews.reason: The aerial embodied benchmark is useful domain evidence, but its main contribution is a benchmark/task formulation rather than a new general AI-system ownership or control contract. It remains contextual until a later cross-domain evaluation chain changes Ch26 or Ch66.
